question: A recent survey by the European Cockpit Association (ECA), involving 7 200 pilots from 32 countries, raises serious concerns about aviation safety. The findings show that more than 76 % of pilots experienced at least one microsleep while operating an aircraft in the previous four weeks. More than half admitted to flying when tired.

1 What is particularly worrying is that many pilots avoid reporting their fatigue out of fear of how the airlines could respond. Given that crew fatigue poses a direct risk to human life, can the Commission say: 1.
Does it intend to tighten controls on the implementation of European rules on flight and rest times for crews?
What measures does it intend to take to ensure that pilots can report cases of fatigue without fear of retaliation and that passenger safety remains an absolute priority?
